Button.notes: Direct mapping. Both are standard button components with similar functionality. MUI Button supports variant (text/contained/outlined), size, color, and other properties.

CheckBox.notes: Direct mapping (case difference). Both allow users to select one or more items from a set. MUI Checkbox supports indeterminate state and FormControlLabel wrapper.

Grid.notes: Functional mapping. Both provide layout containers for arranging elements. MUI Box is a generic, theme-aware container with access to CSS utilities. Use Box with sx prop to implement grid layouts using CSS Grid or Flexbox. For simple row/column layouts, use display: 'grid' with gridTemplateColumns, or use flexbox with flexDirection, gap, etc.

Menu.notes: Direct mapping. Both display a list of choices on temporary surfaces. MUI Menu requires anchorEl to control position and supports anchorOrigin and transformOrigin for position adjustment.

RadioButton.notes: Direct mapping. Both allow users to select one option from a set. MUI uses RadioGroup to wrap multiple Radio components and supports FormControlLabel and error display.

Slider.notes: Direct mapping. Both allow users to make selections from a range of values. MUI Slider supports continuous and discrete modes, range selection, custom marks, and vertical orientation.

StackPanel.notes: Functional mapping. Both arrange elements vertically or horizontally and manage spacing. MUI Stack uses spacing prop to control spacing and supports divider and responsive values.

TabControl.notes: Functional mapping. Both organize and allow navigation between different views. MUI Tabs requires Tab child components and supports scrollable, vertical, icon variants, etc.

TextBox.notes: Functional mapping. Both allow users to enter and edit text. MUI TextField is more feature-rich, supporting variant (outlined/filled/standard), multiline, select, helperText, error, etc.

ToolTip.notes: Direct mapping (case difference). Both display informative text on hover/focus. MUI Tooltip supports 12 placement options, arrow, delay, follow cursor, etc.

ComboBox.notes: Functional mapping. Both allow users to select one item from a dropdown list. MUI Select requires MenuItem child components and supports multiple, native, error, helperText. For autocomplete functionality, use Autocomplete component.

ContextMenu.notes: Functional mapping. Both display context-sensitive menu options. MUI Menu implements context menu through anchorEl and onContextMenu event.

DataGrid.notes: Functional mapping. Both display sets of data in a structured, scannable format. MUI Table requires TableContainer, TableHead, TableBody, TableRow, TableCell child components and supports sorting, selection, pagination, sticky headers.

Expander.notes: Functional mapping. Both let users show and hide sections of related content. MUI Accordion requires AccordionSummary and AccordionDetails child components and supports defaultExpanded, disabled, unmountOnExit.

Label.notes: Functional mapping. Both display text labels. MUI Typography provides more typographic control, supporting variant (h1-h6, body1, body2, etc.), component, color, align, and other properties.

ListBox.notes: Functional mapping. Both display continuous, vertical indexes of items. MUI List requires ListItem or ListItemButton child components and supports ListItemIcon, ListItemText, ListItemAvatar, selected, dense, virtualization.
ListBox.usage_example:
import Box from '@mui/material/Box';
import List from '@mui/material/List';
import ListItem from '@mui/material/ListItem';
import ListItemButton from '@mui/material/ListItemButton';
import ListItemIcon from '@mui/material/ListItemIcon';
import ListItemText from '@mui/material/ListItemText';
import Divider from '@mui/material/Divider';
import InboxIcon from '@mui/icons-material/Inbox';
import DraftsIcon from '@mui/icons-material/Drafts';

export default function BasicList() {
  return (
    <Box sx={{ width: '100%', maxWidth: 360, bgcolor: 'background.paper' }}>
      <nav aria-label="main mailbox folders">
        <List>
          <ListItem disablePadding>
            <ListItemButton>
              <ListItemIcon>
                <InboxIcon />
              </ListItemIcon>
              <ListItemText primary="Inbox" />
            </ListItemButton>
          </ListItem>
          <ListItem disablePadding>
            <ListItemButton>
              <ListItemIcon>
                <DraftsIcon />
              </ListItemIcon>
              <ListItemText primary="Drafts" />
            </ListItemButton>
          </ListItem>
        </List>
      </nav>
      <Divider />
      <nav aria-label="secondary mailbox folders">
        <List>
          <ListItem disablePadding>
            <ListItemButton>
              <ListItemText primary="Trash" />
            </ListItemButton>
          </ListItem>
          <ListItem disablePadding>
            <ListItemButton component="a" href="#simple-list">
              <ListItemText primary="Spam" />
            </ListItemButton>
          </ListItem>
        </List>
      </nav>
    </Box>
  );
}

ListView.notes: Functional mapping (list view mode). Both display continuous, vertical indexes of items. For grid/details view, consider using Table component. MUI List supports ListItemIcon, ListItemText, selected, dense.

Panel.notes: Functional mapping. Both serve as generic container components for layout. MUI Box provides sx prop to access theme-aware CSS utilities and supports component prop to change underlying HTML element.

PasswordBox.notes: Functional mapping. Use TextField with type='password'. MUI TextField supports InputAdornment for password visibility toggle.

Popup.notes: Functional mapping. Both display content on top of another element. MUI Popover is built on Modal, blocks scroll and click away, and requires anchorEl to control position.

ProgressBar.notes: Functional mapping. Use CircularProgress or LinearProgress. MUI Progress supports indeterminate and determinate variants, buffer, custom colors and sizes.

RepeatButton.notes: Functional mapping. Use Button and implement repeat functionality through onClick handlers with setInterval. MUI Button supports loading state and disabled prop.

Separator.notes: Functional mapping. Both provide visual separation between elements. MUI Divider supports variant (fullWidth/inset/middle), orientation (horizontal/vertical), flexItem, and can add child elements (e.g., Chip).

TextBlock.notes: Functional mapping. Both display read-only text content with typographic styling. MUI Typography provides more typographic control, supporting variant, component, color, align, gutterBottom, and other properties.

ToolBar.notes: Functional mapping. Use AppBar with Toolbar component to implement toolbar functionality. MUI AppBar supports position (static/fixed/sticky/relative/absolute), color, elevation, scroll behavior.

Border.notes: Functional mapping. Use Box with sx prop to set border styling. MUI Box supports border, borderRadius, borderColor, and other CSS properties.

GroupBox.notes: Functional mapping. Use Paper or Card component with title/header to implement grouped content. MUI Paper supports elevation, variant (outlined), square. Card provides CardHeader, CardContent, CardActions child components.

ScrollViewer.notes: Functional mapping. Use Box with sx prop to set overflow styling. MUI Box supports overflow, overflowX, overflowY, maxHeight, maxWidth, and other properties.

RichTextBox.notes: Basic mapping. Use TextField with multiline prop. MUI TextField supports minRows, maxRows. For rich text editing, consider using third-party libraries like react-quill or draft-js.

WrapPanel.notes: Functional mapping. Use Box with sx prop to set flexbox wrap styling. MUI Box supports display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap, and other properties.

DockPanel.notes: Functional mapping. Use Box with sx prop to set flexbox layout styling. MUI Box supports flexDirection, justifyContent, alignItems, and other flexbox properties.

Canvas.notes: Functional mapping. Use Box with sx prop to set absolute positioning styling. MUI Box supports position: 'absolute', top, left, right, bottom, zIndex, and other properties.

StatusBar.notes: Functional mapping. Use AppBar with position='fixed' and bottom positioning. MUI AppBar supports position, sx={{ bottom: 0 }} to achieve status bar effect.

TreeView.notes: Basic mapping. Use nested List components. MUI List supports nested structure but requires manual implementation of expand/collapse logic. For advanced tree functionality, consider using third-party libraries like @mui/x-tree-view.
